And it's done on a state-by-state basis. So there's a very good chance it would be very conservative. And what would come out of it would be very conservative. Now, some great scholars on the left, like Larry Lessig at Harvard in Sandy Levinson at the University of Texas have said, we should do that. Progressors should do that. What I am saying is that's a very difficult conversation. What can be done is you can, without completely redoing the Constitution, fix a number of problems through the normal route, which you call it the normal route, that's the only route that's ever been used, which is through Congress. Two thirds of both houses and then three quarters of the states ratified. So at ACS, I'm going to lead an effort to educate the public on and particularly lawyers on, you know, what's the history of these constitutional amendments? What can be done? What is dangerous? What is that we might want to avoid? I think this is a coming crisis. And it's also an opportunity.
